description:
Voids a transaction: QuickBooks keeps it, with its amounts and its lines' quantities at zero and "VOID: " in front of its memo, while deleting one removes it completely. A voided invoice keeps its number and reads back as paid. An invoice that payments paid can be voided too: each payment stays, and what it had applied to the invoice becomes its unused payment, to apply elsewhere or refund (observed on QuickBooks Enterprise 24.0, 2026-10-10).

Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3150 missing_element, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required

include_qbxml.description: Also return the qbXML this compiles to, for debugging. Not part of the v2 request.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

txn_id.description: `txn_id` is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests.

txn_void_type.description: The type of transaction being voided.

name: execute_txn_void

body.description: The JSON body: the arguments you passed.

headers.description: Send with the request. Resent unchanged when no 201 came back, it answers with the request already queued.

qbxml.description: The qbXML it compiles to. Only with include_qbxml.

webhook.description: JSON Schema of the payload POSTed to webhook_url once QuickBooks answers, with this operation's response_json (data shape and status codes).
